detail.Duties Description: The New York State Office of Information Technology Services (ITS) provides operational support 24 hours a day, 7 days a week, 365 days of the year, supporting more than 4,900 applications for 53 New York State Agencies. Under the direction of a Manager of Information Technology Services 1, the Technology Analyst 1 (AI), SG-23, will design, build, integrate, and validate new AI platforms, applications, and developer capabilities within AI Platform Engineering. Specific duties include, but are not limited to, the following: - Translate approved requirements for seven defined projects into technical designs, delivery backlogs, development tasks, and acceptance criteria: GCP Secure AI Lab, AWS Secure AI Lab, Azure Secure AI Lab, AI Farm, FinOps Product, Kiro Enterprise, and RAG Application. - Design, code, integrate, and test secure applications using Python, C#, .NET, PowerShell, and SQL as appropriate to each project; build application interfaces, database schemas, APIs, and automated deployment pipelines. - Build the GCP Secure AI Lab release against the SAIL BRD, including Terraform provisioning, federated access, Cloud Workstations, collaborative notebooks, approved AI services, and test-data workflows. Implement and validate network isolation, controlled egress, sensitive-data protection, model safeguards, logging, and budget controls. - Design and build AWS and Azure Secure AI Lab implementations, establishing provider-specific infrastructure-as-code, identity, network, developer-tool, and governance integrations. Validate repeatable deployment and approved security boundaries before acceptance. - Build AI Farm capabilities for in-house model development and training, including approved data preparation, reproducible training pipelines, experiment tracking, model evaluation, versioned artifacts, and documented release criteria. - Develop the FinOps Product as an in-house application for monitoring financial operations within CTO and ITS. Implement approved data integrations, validation and reconciliation logic, role-based financial reporting, and user-facing analysis capabilities. - Build Kiro Enterprise enablement tooling for MCP registry publication and validation, license-utilization and right-sizing reports, usage telemetry integrations, and repeatable AWS account configuration. Test the new tooling and integrations against approved enterprise requirements. - Develop the RAG Application, including document ingestion, retrieval, application interfaces, and access controls. Build approved source integrations and automated evaluation workflows; validate retrieval quality, security, and performance against agreed acceptance criteria. - Build reusable platform automation and project integrations with enterprise systems, including Active Directory, SCCM, System Center Orchestrator, databases, and approved cloud services where required by the solution design. - Implement DevSecOps and MLOps delivery pipelines, automated tests, and release controls. Conduct integration, security, performance, and user acceptance testing; correct defects identified during project validation. - Produce architecture diagrams, source code, infrastructure definitions, test evidence, deployment instructions, and knowledge-transfer materials for each completed build. Coordinate release acceptance and transfer completed capabilities to designated service owners. - Coordinate project dependencies and delivery reviews with the Manager of Information Technology Services 1, stakeholders, developers, and security and infrastructure teams. Follow applicable NYS laws, ITS policies, and approved engineering standards throughout design and delivery.

detail.Duties Description: The New York State Department of Financial Services seeks to build an equitable, transparent, and resilient financial system that benefits individuals and supports business. Through engagement, data-driven regulation and policy, and operational excellence, the Department and its employees are responsible for empowering consumers and protecting them from financial harm; ensuring the health of the entities we regulate; driving economic growth in New York through responsible innovation; and preserving the stability of the global financial system. The Department of Financial Services is seeking candidates for the position of Data Analyst 2 in Office of Responsible Artificial Intelligence Safety & Education (RAISE). detail.Duties Description: Executive Division Research and Analytics Department—NYC Data Scientist Reference No. RAD_NYC_DAS_6463 Application Deadline is November 13, 2026 Salary is $116,233 + $4,150 in location pay To be considered for this opportunity, submit a complete application online at https://ag.ny.gov/job-postings/other Goal: The Research and Analytics Department in the Office of the New York State Attorney General (OAG) is seeking candidates for a full-time Data Scientist position. Data Scientists at OAG bring their skills to bear across a wide variety of cases and investigations. The Data Scientist will utilize a vast array of tools to explore datasets, develop new databases, and use statistical modeling to detect anomalies in information pertinent to OAG investigations. The goal of the Data Scientist at OAG is to ensure that our most complicated cases and policy arenas have the benefit of advanced analytical tools, methodologies, and strategic thinking to understand how otherwise elusive trends can be laid bare once we dive into the underlying data. Purview: As part of an innovative team housed in the Executive Division, you will work with senior staff and divisions throughout OAG to support OAG's major initiatives, investigations, and policy development. Our team researches and writes analytical reports garnering national attention, directs multi-million-dollar grant programs, and supports OAG’s major investigations. See for example: lawsuit against auto lender for deceptive practices, preliminary report on NYPD response to Protests, JUUL lawsuit and remediation, opioids lawsuit, lawsuit preserving affordable housing from illegal kickback scheme, and the FCC fake comments report. Utilizing a vast collection of public and confidential information, you will work with data covering the breadth of OAG’s purview building advanced analytic tools to inform investigations that affect the lives of all New Yorkers. Employing over 2,000 people across New York state, OAG is both the “People's Lawyer” and the state's chief legal officer. The Data Scientist will support OAG work in numerous legal and regulatory arenas, including protecting the rights of investors and consumers, coordinating state-wide criminal investigations, promoting civil rights, economic and social justice, encouraging harm-reducing public health strategies, and preserving the state’s environment. The OAG also advises the Executive branch of state government and defends actions and proceedings on behalf of the state. Duties: Data can and does play a pivotal role in decisioning on a wide range of OAG’s work. The Data Scientist will be primarily responsible for: • All aspects of using data to develop and test legal hypotheses, including: o Brainstorming with legal teams on the data required o Acquiring data through public sources and assisting legal teams to acquire data from confidential sources to ensure the delivery of data sufficient for investigation o Testing data for reliability o Distilling and incorporating relevant academic and other analytical research o Developing and executing appropriate methodologies for data exploration and analysis o Clearly communicating findings verbally and through written reports and visualizations, including relevant limitations o Continuously updating analysis in the face of feedback and new data o Quantifying uncertainty in analytical findings • Working closely with legal teams on all the aspects above and providing guidance and recommendations on decision making around data • Additional responsibilities may include: o Developing predictive modeling to detect anomalies o Developing or programming new databases or data tools o Writing fact and expert reports for submission to the court and defending analysis and findings in depositions o Helping to maintain and improve the team’s shared computational infrastructure o Staying informed of the latest advances in data tools and techniques and sharing newfound skills with the team o Performing other duties as requested

detail.Title: State EMS SIGNAL Systems Unit Coordinator (Business Systems Analyst 1 Health) (NY HELPS) - 52411

detail.Duties Description: The SIGNAL System Unit Coordinator (Business Systems Analyst 1 Health) serves as a full-performance business systems analyst for the Strategic Incident & Geospatial Notification, Analytics, and Logistics system, known as SIGNAL, the Division’s statewide emergency management information environment. SIGNAL includes Juvare WebEOC, EMResource, EMTrack, and related applications, dashboards, data exchanges, and integrations used to support health and medical preparedness, facility incident reporting, statewide situational awareness, incident notifications and information exchange, resource coordination, patient and asset tracking, planned-event operations, and emergency response. Working under the general direction of the SIGNAL System Unit Manager, the coordinator conducts business systems analysis and supports the design, configuration, testing, implementation, reporting, training, and continuous improvement of SIGNAL capabilities. The position works with the State Medical Operations Coordination Center, State EMS Task Force, Division emergency management programs, Department partners, health care facilities, EMS providers, local health departments, emergency management organizations, information technology staff, vendors, and other authorized system users. Work involving regulatory programs is limited to emergency management functions or information needed for preparedness and response and does not include administration of routine licensing, certification, investigation, or enforcement systems. The position performs the full range of business systems analysis activities for multiple interrelated emergency management applications, workflows, data sets, reports, integrations, and user groups. Assignments require the coordinator to select and apply appropriate analytical techniques; evaluate current and proposed business processes; elicit and reconcile differing stakeholder requirements; translate emergency management needs into functional requirements, data specifications, workflows, reports, and acceptance criteria; and assess how proposed changes may affect downstream processes, notifications, data quality, access permissions, reporting, and system integrations. The coordinator independently completes assigned analyses and implementations within approved SIGNAL governance, configuration, security, documentation, and change-management standards and refers significant policy, system architecture, cybersecurity, contractual, or enterprise-priority matters to the SIGNAL System Unit Manager. Errors in requirements, configuration, testing, data definitions, reporting, or implementation may result in incomplete or misleading situational awareness, delayed incident reporting or notifications, inaccurate facility, patient, or resource information, disrupted emergency management workflows, inappropriate access to sensitive information, or reduced system effectiveness during an incident. The work requires sound judgment to balance operational urgency, stakeholder needs, data quality, usability, information protection, continuity, technical feasibility, and long-term system sustainability, including during emergency activations when requirements and priorities may change rapidly. The coordinator exercises ownership and accountability for assigned business systems analysis activities and for the accuracy, quality, completeness, and timely delivery of associated work products. Major Functions and Associated Duties: Emergency Management Business Process Analysis and Requirements Development Conducts full-range business systems analysis for assigned SIGNAL initiatives and enhancements supporting statewide health and medical emergency management; Elicits business, functional, data, reporting, access, and user requirements through interviews, facilitated work sessions, observation, surveys, document review, analysis of exercises and actual incidents, and review of existing system use; Maps and documents current or “as-is” processes and develops proposed future or “to-be” process models for facility incident reporting, status reporting, situational awareness, incident notifications, resource requests, patient and asset tracking, deployment coordination, planned-event support, and related emergency management functions; Identifies business-process deficiencies, duplicated activities, data gaps, inconsistent practices, control weaknesses, and opportunities for standardization, automation, or improved information exchange; Develops business cases, business requirements documents, functional specifications, use cases, process diagrams, data definitions, validation rules, notification requirements, report specifications, role requirements, and acceptance criteria; Analyzes requested changes to determine the underlying business need, affected users, operational impact, dependencies, constraints, risks, and alignment with approved SIGNAL governance and emergency management objectives; Reconciles differing stakeholder requirements and recommends process, configuration, reporting, training, or procedural solutions to the SIGNAL System Unit Manager; Maintains requirements traceability, decision records, and controlled documentation throughout the system development and implementation life cycle. SIGNAL Solution Configuration, Validation, and Implementation Configures approved business-facing components of Juvare WebEOC, EMResource, EMTrack, and related SIGNAL applications within delegated functional authority, including boards, forms, data views, fields, status options, resource elements, workflows, business rules, alerts, notifications, dashboards, and reports; Develops prototypes, mock-ups, and configuration models to demonstrate proposed solutions and obtain validation from program subject-matter experts and affected users; Translates approved requirements into functional configuration instructions for vendors, information technology staff, or other technical personnel when a change requires programming, infrastructure modification, technical security administration, or integration development outside the position’s assigned authority; Develops test plans, test data, scenarios, expected results, and acceptance measures addressing normal operations, emergency conditions, exception handling, data validation, role-based functions, and system dependencies; Performs functional, regression, integration, usability, role-based access, and user-acceptance testing to determine whether solutions satisfy approved requirements and operate as intended; Documents defects, unmet requirements, configuration errors, workflow failures, and implementation risks; Coordinates corrective action with appropriate program, vendor, or technical personnel and verifies completed corrections through retesting; Assesses the effects of vendor releases, upgrades, configuration changes, and system modifications on established workflows, reports, data exchanges, permissions, and user functions; Coordinates assigned implementation activities, including readiness reviews, configuration migration, documentation updates, user communications, training preparation, deployment support, and post-implementation monitoring; Maintains configuration inventories, change records, test results, implementation documentation, and version histories. Emergency Management Data Quality, Reporting, and Performance Analysis Develops, configures, or specifies routine and ad hoc reports, dashboards, maps, data visualizations, alerts, extracts, and performance measures supporting statewide situational awareness, health care preparedness, incident management, resource coordination, patient tracking, response operations, and executive decision support; Applies approved data definitions, reporting conventions, validation rules, source-system responsibilities, and quality-control procedures to information collected, processed, displayed, or exchanged through SIGNAL; Monitors data completeness, consistency, accuracy, timeliness, workflow completion, and system utilization to identify configuration, process, integration, training, or user-support needs; Investigates data discrepancies by tracing information through forms, workflows, reports, dashboards, interfaces, and source systems and coordinates corrective action with the appropriate business owner, system administrator, vendor, or technical staff; Analyzes system use, reporting participation, data-quality trends, workflow performance, and recurring deficiencies and prepares findings and recommendations for the SIGNAL System Unit Manager; Supports the development and modification of approved data exchanges and system integrations by documenting business rules, source and destination fields, mappings, triggers, validation requirements, error conditions, and expected outputs; Validates integration results and automated data flows to verify that exchanged information satisfies the approved emergency management purpose and maintains data integrity; Maintains data dictionaries, metadata, report specifications, dashboard documentation, recurring reporting schedules, and quality-assurance records; Handles sensitive facility, operational, resource, and patient-tracking information in accordance with Department policies and approved access and information-handling standards. User Readiness, Functional Support, and Emergency Operations Support Provides functional assistance to authorized internal and external SIGNAL users by analyzing reported issues and determining whether they arise from business processes, application configuration, data, functional access, training, system use, or technical conditions; Resolves functional issues within assigned authority and coordinates infrastructure, account, cybersecurity, programming, integration, or vendor-product issues with the appropriate technical administrator, information technology staff, or vendor support resource; Defines business requirements for user roles and permissions and validates that proposed access supports approved emergency management functions, separation of duties, and information-protection requirements; Develops and maintains user guides, standard operating procedures, job aids, frequently asked questions, training presentations, exercises, demonstrations, and other instructional materials; Conducts training for Division staff, Department partners, health care facilities, EMS agencies, local health departments, emergency management organizations, and other authorized users; Coordinates user-readiness and change-management activities for new workflows, system enhancements, upgrades, reports, and data requirements; Collects and analyzes user feedback, support requests, system-use patterns, and recurring questions to identify enhancement, communication, documentation, or training needs; Supports exercises, planned events, emergency activations, and continuity operations by implementing approved incident-specific forms, boards, workflows, displays, notifications, reports, dashboards, and user-access requirements; Monitors SIGNAL functionality, workflow completion, and data flow during assigned emergency-support periods and promptly escalates issues that may affect situational awareness, incident notifications, patient or resource tracking, or response coordination; Documents system-related observations and lessons learned and develops recommendations for configuration, workflow, reporting, documentation, training, or procedural improvements following exercises and activations.

detail.Title: Special Advisor to the Superintendent for Technology Policy (Special Assistant, NS)
detail.Duties Description: The New York State Department of Financial Services seeks to build an equitable, transparent, and resilient financial system that benefits individuals and supports business. Through engagement, data-driven regulation and policy, and operational excellence, the Department and its employees are responsible for empowering consumers and protecting them from financial harm; ensuring the health of the entities we regulate; driving economic growth in New York through responsible innovation; and preserving the stability of the global financial system. The Department of Financial Services is seeking candidates for the position of Special Advisor to the Superintendent for Technology Policy in the Executive Division. Under the direction of the Superintendent of the Department of Financial Services, the incumbent of this position will provide strategic counsel, subject matter expertise, and serve as lead implementer of identified priorities. detail.Duties Description: The State University of New York, or SUNY, is the largest comprehensive system of public higher education in the United States, with 64 colleges and universities spanning the state from Long Island to the Adirondacks to Buffalo. SUNY System Administration employees, based in Albany and New York City, provide critical support for SUNY campuses, employees, and students to advance SUNY's mission of providing high-quality, affordable higher education for all. Across a wide range of roles, from finance and legal counsel to student support, academic affairs, IT, admissions, and more, our employees work toward advancing the four priority pillars established by SUNY Chancellor John B. King Jr. and the SUNY Board of Trustees: student success; research and scholarship; diversity, equity, and inclusion; and economic development and upward mobility. SUNY System Administration is a mission-driven workplace with robust New York State benefits including health insurance, retirement, time off, and paid family leave. The Director of SUNY Information Technology Optimization and Engagement provides leadership for projects and portfolio management across the SUNY Office of Information Technology under the direction of the Chief Information Officer (CIO). The Director leads and supports a project management office responsible for establishing consistent project management policies and practices, coordinating work across the OIT portfolio, and providing leadership with clear information about project status, costs, schedules, risks, dependencies, resource needs, and expected outcomes. The Director is responsible for ensuring IT projects are aligned with SUNY's strategic goals and portfolio management priorities driving alignment and engagement across 64 campuses and SUNY hospitals for campus and central administration technology operations. Track, analyze, and report on all MPTV programs, including but not limited to Film, Independent, Post, Music & Theatrical incentive programs. • Manage data extraction, database maintenance, and analytical reporting, including preparation of memos and briefing materials for regular meetings, monthly and quarterly reports, and industry stakeholder engagement activities.
